topic: DP-3T: The Privacy-First Way to Trace Infections
target_audience: University students in Computer Science or Public Health

sections.title: The Privacy Dilemma (0:45)
lecture_lines: How do we trace infections without tracking people?
Traditional tracing creates a central map of movements.
DP-3T offers a decentralized, privacy-first alternative.
animations: Alice (#3498DB) and Bob (#E67E22) dots moving on a dark background.
A red eye (#E74C3C) representing a central server appears, watching them.
The eye disappears, replaced by a "Privacy First" shield (#3498DB) icon.
Alice and Bob exchange glowing yellow (#F1C40F) dots representing ephemeral IDs.
The title "DP-3T" (#FFFFFF) appears in the center.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Digital Shredder (Hashing) (0:45)
lecture_lines: A secret seed generates unique, temporary IDs.
Hashing is like a mathematical one-way blender.
IDs are public, but the seed stays hidden.
animations: A seed icon (#E67E22) labeled "Secret Seed" enters a blender graphic (#95A5A6).
Three different alphanumeric strings (#1ABC9C) emerge from the blender.
A red arrow (#E74C3C) pointing back from IDs to Seed is crossed out to show one-way hashing.

sections.title: Phase 1: The Daily Handshake (1:00)
lecture_lines: Phones broadcast temporary IDs via Bluetooth signals.
Alice’s phone generates a new ID every fifteen minutes.
Bob’s phone records Alice’s ID in a local log.
No locations or names are ever exchanged.
These secret handshakes stay only on your device.
animations: Alice (#3498DB) and Bob (#E67E22) icons stay within a circular Bluetooth range (#5DADE2).
A 15-minute clock icon (#FFFFFF) ticks once.
A yellow code "ID-A" (#F1C40F) floats from Alice to Bob's phone.
Bob's phone displays a list adding "ID-A" into its storage (#2ECC71).
The clock ticks again; Alice sends "ID-B" (#F1C40F) and Bob's list updates.

sections.title: Phase 2: The Diagnosis Key (1:00)
lecture_lines: If Alice tests positive, she voluntarily shares her seed.
She only uploads seeds for her contagious days.
The central server receives these diagnosis keys anonymously.
The server acts like a public bulletin board.
It never learns who Alice actually met.
animations: Alice icon (#3498DB) changes color to red (#E74C3C) with a "+" symbol.
An arrow carries the "Secret Seed" (#E67E22) from Alice to a cloud icon (#FFFFFF).
The cloud icon displays the seed but no personal data or EphIDs.

sections.title: Phase 3: Local Matching & Alert (1:00)
lecture_lines: Bob’s phone downloads new diagnosis keys daily.
It locally regenerates the IDs from those seeds.
The phone checks for matches in its local log.
A match triggers a private exposure alert.
All matching happens locally, never on the server.
animations: Bob's phone (#E67E22) pulls the "Secret Seed" (#E67E22) from the cloud (#FFFFFF).
The phone generates IDs locally using a blender graphic (#95A5A6).
A match between local "ID-A" and generated IDs is highlighted in yellow (#F1C40F).
A red "Exposure Alert" (#E74C3C) banner appears on Bob's phone.
Bob icon (#E67E22) pulses to indicate notification received.

sections.title: Conclusion: The Decentralized Win (0:30)
lecture_lines: DP-3T keeps sensitive data off the central server.
Users remain anonymous dots on a hidden map.
Privacy and public health can coexist through decentralization.
animations: A split screen shows the Server (#FFFFFF) with seeds and User (#3498DB) with names.
A grey wall (#95A5A6) between them shows no identity data crossing to the server.
Text "Decentralized Trust" (#2ECC71) appears in the center.
